text:
maria_ng: Hey — hitting a Windows + Python quickstart issue. Fresh venv on Win10, Python 3.11.3. First call to the Python SDK fails with an SSL handshake error on our corp network. sample app is unmodified. Anyone seen this?

alex_k: Ugh, yep seen similar when corp MITM proxies are in play. Can you paste the full error and a minimal repro?

maria_ng: Stack trace (trimmed):
```
ssl.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] certificate verify failed: unable to get local issuer certificate (_ssl.c:997)
  File "...\\site-packages\\httpx\\_client.py", line 730, in send
    raise SSLHandshakeError from e
```
Not using pyinstaller or freezing — just normal venv. Requests and httpx are latest.

sam_w: Two quick checks: 1) is certifi installed in that venv? 2) what's ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION on that Python build? Run:
```
python -c \"import certifi, ssl; print(certifi.where()); print(ssl.OPENSSL_VERSION)\"
```

maria_ng: certifi.where() points to `C:\\Users\\maria\\venv\\Lib\\site-packages\\certifi\\cacert.pem` and openssl is \"OpenSSL 1.1.1k  25 Mar 2021\"

gina_ops: If your corp uses an intercepting proxy you'll need the company CA in the bundle. On Windows sometimes the system store is used by apps, but Python uses certifi file. Setting REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE or SSL_CERT_FILE to point to a combined bundle (certifi + corpCA.pem) usually fixes it.

alex_k: For the SDK we currently accept `verify=` passed through to httpx, but our quickstart doesn't show how to set it on Windows. You can do: `client = RedwoodClient(api_key=..., verify=\"C:\\\\path\\\\to\\\\combined.pem\")`.

maria_ng: Tried REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE and SSL_CERT_FILE with the combined bundle, still flakey. Also seeing this only on async client (AsyncClient) — sync client works fine. Typing note: mypy complains about missing overloads for async call patterns in the SDK stubs.

sam_w: Two separate things: async handshake difference might be due to asyncio event loop policy on Windows (Proactor event loop + winssl oddities). What version of httpx/anyio/httpcore? Also can you share minimal async snippet?

maria_ng: httpx==0.24.0, httpcore==0.16.0, anyio==3.6.2. Snippet:
```python
import asyncio
from redwood import AsyncRedwoodClient

async def main():
    c = AsyncRedwoodClient(api_key=..., verify=\"C:\\\\temp\\\\combined.pem\")
    await c.generate(\"hello\")

asyncio.run(main())
```
Error happens inside httpcore during TLS handshake.

gina_ops: If httpcore is using the system TLS backend that's sometimes linked against different OpenSSL / SChannel on Windows. Could you try forcing httpx to use the same cert file by setting environment var `SSL_CERT_FILE` and verifying with a curl or python `requests` call to the same endpoint?

alex_k: Also note: when people bundle apps (pyinstaller) certifi's data file often gets omitted. For that you'd add `--add-data \"<path to certifi>\\cacert.pem;certifi\"`. Not your case but worth calling out in docs.

maria_ng: Good point. I validated with `python -c \"import ssl, certifi; print(open(certifi.where()).read()[:80])\"` and the combined bundle is loaded. Curl to the endpoint using that bundle works. So it's something with httpcore + Windows async handshake when a custom bundle is provided.

sam_w: Filing a bug & feature request: 1) Bug — async TLS verify path on Windows when a custom `verify` path is used. 2) Feature — expose an explicit `root_certs` helper and document Windows quickstart steps (env vars + combined bundle). Also add typing stubs for Async client overloads.

devex-bot: Created issue GH #3245: \"Windows async TLS verification with custom cert bundle + typing stubs for Async client\" (https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood/issues/3245) :robot_face:

alex_k: Thanks @devex-bot. I'll pick up the docs PR for the quickstart (Windows troubleshooting section) and add a short note about `SSL_CERT_FILE` vs `REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE` and pyinstaller caveats. :thumbsup:

maria_ng: Awesome — after switching to the alpha SDK with a small httpcore downgrade the handshake stopped failing. Will post exact repro steps in the GH issue. Can we also get a short note in the Python quickstart about typing/myPy expectations for Async client? I had to add `# type: ignore` in a few places.

alex_k: Will add a typing note and try to scope the stub fixes. Thanks for the repro, @maria_ng — helpful.

maria_ng: Thanks everyone!
